nodes.title: Prompt + the views for this shot
Read me
widgets_values:
## 5. View sets: a billboard of angles
A **view set** is a RefCap holding many views of one subject, each with the angle it was seen from, plus an optional orbit video. It is H3's counterpart of a TURNtable billboard, the Blender plane that swaps turntable frames by camera angle. H3 can't pick a reference by angle on its own, so **H3 RefCap Replay View Set** picks the views for your shot before encoding, then replays them exactly as native references.

**Build (top node, muted)**
1. Put the turntable frames in a folder under `ComfyUI/input/`. Files sort the way TURNtable Viewer sorts them, so the same folder works in both.
2. Set `view_folder`. Leave `yaws` empty for evenly spaced frames: frame i at i x 360/N + `frame_offset_degrees`, mirrored by `reverse_direction`, as in the add-on. Or give one angle per view.
3. Optional: `orbit_folder` (or `orbit` frames) stores a turntable clip as a video reference. Set `orbit_length` to the length you will render; H3 cuts a reference video to the clip's length.
   **Clips and audio (version 3):** `clip_2` / `clip_3` (frames or folders) store up to three clips; `orbit_audio`, `clip_2_audio`, `clip_3_audio` store their soundtracks; `audio_1..3` store standalone audio references (a voice, music, ambience). Any audio needs the `audio_vae`. Audio is stored as the audio VAE's latent only: the text encoder never sees audio, so that latent is exactly what the native node hands the DiT. A soundtrack is not cut to the render's length (the native node doesn't either); trim it first with *Trim Audio Duration* if it should be. *Load Video* + *Get Video Components* give a clip's frames and soundtrack; *Load Audio* also reads audio from a video file.
4. Unmute the node (Ctrl+M), queue once, mute it again. Refresh the browser so the file appears in `viewset`.

**Generate**
- `select` = `nearest`: `target_yaws` are the angles the shot shows (0 front, 90 side, 180 back); each takes its nearest view. `count` adds more views near those angles (0 = one per angle). `all` and `indices` choose directly.
- At most 9 views per shot, the native reference node's limit. A 1024 px view costs about 1,024 tokens on every step.
- `orbit` adds clip 1 as `<Video 1>`; `more_clips` (e.g. `2,3`) adds the other clips; `audios` (`all` or numbers) adds the standalone audio references.
- The **Label guide** says which view each `<Picture i>` is and its angle, and which clip or audio each `<Video k>` and `<Audio j>` is. Name the angles in the prompt, e.g. `<Subject 1> is the man in <Picture 1> (front view) and <Picture 2> (side view)`.

**Measured** (one Multiface subject, 3 shots x 3 seeds, ~5,000 reference tokens per arm):

| references | face similarity |
|---|---|
| 5 front and 3/4 views, 1024 px | **0.724** |
| 9 views around the head, 736 px | 0.719 |
| a 56-frame orbit as `<Video 1>`, 544 px | 0.718 |
| 5 views chosen for the shot, 1024 px | 0.712 |
| none | 0.022 |

- Spending the budget on angles instead of detail **did not** improve facial identity: the four are within 0.012.
- Coverage wins only where the head is turned furthest (|yaw| >= 70 degrees: +0.04 for the ring, +0.06 for the orbit) and loses slightly below that.
- What it does fix is **the back of the head**, which face metrics can't score: the subject's hair clip, visible only in her side and back views, appeared in 9 of 9 coverage clips and 0 of 3 front-only ones.
- The orbit is also the cheapest per clip (~51 s against ~84 s): the text encoder sees a video reference at 2 fps.

**So use a view set** for shots that turn away from the camera or show the back of the head. For ordinary front-facing shots, five sharp 1024 px front and 3/4 views do as well.

**Settings in these workflows** follow ComfyUI's MiniMax H3 reference-to-video template: the ref2va model with its 4-step Lightning LoRA, 4 steps, `res_multistep` + `simple`, 608x352. For the base model, bypass the *Lightning LoRA* node and use 20 steps. The measurements quoted here ran on a community H3 turbo finetune (shift 6/3, 8 steps) on a 12 GB GPU. Raise the size and length for final renders; the reference tokens ride through every step, so more photos and larger captures cost time.

nodes.title: Prompt guide
widgets_values:
## Writing the prompt
H3's reference mode reads a structured prompt. The photos are labelled in order: `<Picture 1>` ... `<Picture N>`, where N is the number of photos in the RefCap.

```
subject_definitions:
<Subject 1> is the woman in <Picture 1>, <Picture 2> and <Picture 3>, a white woman in her mid-twenties with dark brown, wavy, shoulder-length hair.

summary:
[reference generation] <Subject 1> sits at a sunlit cafe table and smiles at the camera.

retention_analysis:
<Subject 1> (appears in [Shot 1]): fully_preserved - the woman's facial identity and hairstyle are retained.

detailed_description:
The target video is a realistic, full-color cinematic shot with warm daylight.
[Shot 1] A medium close-up shows <Subject 1>, wearing a navy t-shirt, ...

overall_soundscape:
Gentle street ambience.

non_diegetic_music:
N/A
```

**Tips**
- Describe age, gender and hair, and **say the outfit and action you want**. The photos supply the face; the prompt supplies everything else.
- Don't count on a name. The tests never used one.
- More detail in `detailed_description` (camera, lighting, motion, sound) gives better shots. MiniMax's guide suggests 350-500 words for final renders.
- Official format guide: MiniMax-H3 `docs/VIDEO_PROMPT_WRITING_GUIDE_ref_en.md`.
